Hon. Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND Francisco Gold Condomini ND LVCAL EDSA cor. Mapagmahal St., CVG LEAS D Quezon City SIGNATVRE 'ATE: LEGAL SERVI 0 camu RO. Legal Opinion No. 79 s. 2011 22 2011 ATTY. ROMEO M. ACOP, MNSA oyee Representative, 2nd District, Antipolo City HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES Batasan Complex, Quezon City Dear Rep. Romeo M. Acop: This has reference to your letter seeking the opinion of this Department regarding the legal implication of a reapportionment of the present two (2) districts of Antipolo City on the membership to the City Council and Provincial Board if and when a law is passed creating a third legislative district therein. For easy reference, we quote your queries as follows: 1) Does the creation of a new legislative district in Antipolo City ih addition to its existing two (2) legislative districts legally entail an increase in the membership of the City Council such that additional seats will be allocated to the new legislative district? If so, what will be the apportionment of seats among the legislative districts in the city? Presently, the City Council has 16 councilors with 8 elected at large in each legislative district. 2) Does the creation of a new legislative district in Antipolo City in addition to its existing two (2) legislative districts legally entail an increase in the membership of the Provincial Board such that an additional seat will be allocated to the new legislative district? If not so, will the new legislative district be alloted a seat from the existing number of seats in the Provincial Board among the legislative districts in the province? At present, the Province of Rizal has IO Board Members with 4 each from the the 2 legislative districts of the province and 1 each from the 2 legislative districts of the city. 3) If the preceding queries are resolved in the affirmative, what will be the legal effect on the term limits of incumbent Provincial Board and City Council members, as well as incumbent representatives affected by the district reapportionment who will seek seats in the new legislative district? This Department's Opinion: Legislative apportionment is defined by Black's Law Dictionary as the determination of the number of representatives which a State, county or other subdivision may send to a legislative body. It is the allocation of seats in a legislative body in proportion to the population; the drawing of voting district lines so as to equalize population and voting power among the districts. Reapportionment, on the other

hand, is the realignment or change in legislative districts brought about by changes in population and mandated by the constitutional requirement of equality of representation. (Rogelio Bagabuyo vs. Commission on Elections, G.R. No. 176970, 08 December 2008) The objective of legal apportionment is to make a legislative district sufficiently represented so that the people can be effectively heard. As above stated, the aim of legislative apportionment is "to equalize population and voting power among districts." Hence, emphasis is given to the number of people represented; the uniform and progressive ratio to be observed among the representative districts; and accessibility and commonality of interests in terms of each district being, as far as practicable, continuous, compact and adjacent territory. In terms of the people represented, every city with at least 250,000 people and every province (irrespective of population) is entitled to one representative. In this sense, legislative districts, on the one hand, and provinces and cities, on the other, relate and interface with each other. (Rogelio Bagabuyo vs. commjsston on Elections, G.R. No. 176970, 08 December 2008) The discussion above shows, among others, that a legislative disctrict is not a territorial nor political subdivision through which the functions of the government are carried out, unlike the local government units ( provinces, cities, municipalities, and the barangays). This equality of representation is anchored on Section 5, Article VI (Legislative Department) of the 1987 Constitution, and we cite paragraph (3) thereof: "(3) Each legislative district shall comprise, as far as practicable, contiguous, compact, and adjacent territory. Each city, with a population of at least two hundred fifty thousand, or each province, shall have at least one representative. " (emphasis supplied) Therefore, a legislative act or measure that will provide for a third legislative district does not divide Antipolo City into separate political units. If the law would be passed for said purpose, Antipolo City would have a third congressman representing at least 250,000 inhabitants or population of the said city. Plainly stated, a city must first meet a population minimum of 250,000 in order to be similarly entitled. (Aquino and Robredo vs Commission on Elections, G.R. No. 189793, 07 April 2010) Opinion to Query I: As held in the aforecited Bagabuyo case, the creation of a third legislative district shall bring about additional Sangguniang Panlungsod seats to be voted for, citing RA 6636, "An Act Resetting the Local Elections From November 9, 1987 to January 18, 1988 Amending for this Purpose Executive Order Numbered Two Hundred and Seventy", Section 3 thereof as the basis, to wit: "SECTION 3. Other Cities. — The provision of any law to the contrary notwithstanding the City of Cebu, City of Davao, and anp other city with more than one representative district shall have EIGHT (8) COUNCILORS FOR EACH DISTRICT who shall be residents thereof to be elected by the qualified voters therein, provided that the cities of Cagayan de Oro, Zamboanga, Bacolod, Iloilo and other cities comprising a representative district shall have twelve (12) councilors each and all other cities shall have ten (IO) councilors each to be elected at large by the qualified voters of the said cities: Provided, That in no case shall the present number of councilors according to their charters be reduced". (emphasis supplied) Thus, a third legislative district shall have eight (8) councilors who shall have be residents thereof to be elected by the qualified voters therein.

Opinion to Ouery 2: Necessarily, the membership of the Provincial Board will be increased. As to the apportionment, we cite RA 7166, "An Act Providing for Synchronized National and Local Elections and Forl Electoral Reforms, Authorizing Appropriations Therefor, And For Other Purposes", Section 3(a) thereof, which states: "(a) For provinces with two (2) or more legislative districts, the elective members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall be elected by legislative districts. For this purpose, the number of seats shall be apportioned equitably: Provided, That, if equal division is not possible, the remaining member or members shall be elected in the district or districts with the greater number of population or, if they be the same, with the greater number of voters: Provided further, That, if a legislative district includes a city that does not vote in the election of provincial officials, the Commission on Elections, hereinafter referred to as the Commission, shall allocate the number of seats among the districts in proportion to the population of the constituencies voting for the Sangguniang Panlalawigan " (emphasis supplied) Opinion to Query 3: On the matter of term limits of incumbent elective local officials, the prevailing law thereon applies. Section 8, Article X of the 1987 Constitution and Section 43 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991, in essence, provides that the term of office of elective local officials, except barangay officials, shall be three years and no such official shall serve for more than three consecutive years. Thank you very much and we hope that we have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Very truly yours, JESUS B. DOQUE IV Director III IS: 55/06
